column1: # A multi-node devnet convergence soak: the status samples.
# Four zycordd processes on the dev engine (dev-blake3, no RandomX), five-second
# blocks, eight-block epochs, behind a chaos proxy injecting 15 ms latency,
# 0-35 ms jitter, 0.1% chunk loss and 0.05% chunk severance in both directions,
# while the harness killed and revived nodes and opened partitions. Built with
# -tags zcdguard, so the consensus-state access rules were machine-checked for
# the whole run, and every node was verified to report the guard armed before
# any chaos was applied.
# Regime: TestChaosSoak (55 minutes of chaos, then all but one miner stopped
# and a convergence window). Nodes a, b, c mine; d is outbound-only, the shape a
# home connection has without NAT traversal.
# The run: 191 kills, 379 partitions. It ended
#   converged: 4 nodes at height 1015 on one chain, one tip, one state root
#   settled convergence: height 1007,
#     agreed by 4/4 nodes (a,b,c,d)
#   crossed 126 epoch boundaries
#   billing law: 736 certificate inclusions across 1015 blocks, no duplicates
#   liveness: no node died unbidden (12607 state samples)
# What to read. The columns are seconds since sampling began, the node, whether
# its RPC answered, its height, how many blocks it trailed the highest node at
# that instant, its resident memory, its thread count, its open file
# descriptors, its data directory in kilobytes, and the first eight bytes of its
# tip.
# reachable=false with height 0 is a node the harness had killed and not yet
# restarted; it is the disturbance working, not a defect. The trail column is
# where the latency lives: p50=0, p90=1, p99=2, max=11 blocks across 850
# node-samples, the maximum being a node catching up after a kill.
# On memory: read the FLOOR, not the peak. Go's collector produces a sawtooth,
# so the peak of any one node ratchets and means little -- node c touched 69.6 MB
# at t=1710 and was back to 27.4 MB by t=1755. The floor per ten-minute window
# went 13.3, 17.1, 14.3, 19.4, 23.1, 25.7 MB while the chain went from height 278
# to 1015 and the data directory from 1.5 to 6.7 MB. Memory grew about 1.9x
# while the data it holds grew about 4x, which is a cache tracking a growing
# chain rather than a leak. Threads stayed at 13 and descriptors at 21 for the
# whole run; neither moved with time.
# This machine was running five other test suites throughout, at a load average
# between 8 and 47 on six cores. That inflates every timing here and none of the
# convergence facts: whether four nodes hold one block id at a settled height is
# not something a slow machine answers differently.
